title: Béarnaise Sauce
description: Warm butter emulsified into egg yolks and a sharp tarragon-shallot reduction. The sauce for steak frites.
notes: It holds for an hour in a warm (not hot) place — a thermos is the restaurant trick. If it splits, whisk a spoon of it into a fresh yolk and add the rest slowly.

steps.text: Simmer the white wine vinegar, white wine, shallot, peppercorns, and half the tarragon until reduced to about 2 tablespoons.
steps.tip: Reduce it properly. Too much liquid left and the sauce is sharp and thin.

steps.text: Whisk the reduction with the egg yolks in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water until thick and pale and the whisk leaves trails.
steps.tip: If the yolks start to scramble at the edges, lift the bowl off the heat and keep whisking.

steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in the warm clarified butter in a thin stream until thick and glossy.
Season with salt and stir in the remaining tarragon and the chervil. Serve warm, never hot.
